![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14255499/assets/f154d0638a1fd0d1e4d5f56d1ee374c3c01cb31044b7c62e0205538ea51452a4.png)

We need to create a cylindrical tin with no lid using $12\pi \,{cm}^{2}$ of sheet metal. What is the largest possible volume ${V}_{\text{max}}$ of the cylinder? Do not round the answer.

${V}_{\text{max}}=$
{{field-1}} ${\text{cm}}^{3}$
question.worked_solution:
First, let $r$ be the radius and $h$ be the height of the cylinder.

We wish to maximize the volume

$$
V=\pi {r}^{2}h.
$$

We know that the surface area is fixed at $12\pi \,{cm}^{2},$ so we also have the constraint equation

$$
2\pi rh+\pi {r}^{2}=12\pi .
$$

Now, by making $h$ the subject of the constraint equation, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi rh & =12\pi -\pi {r}^{2} \\ h & =\frac{6}{r}-\frac{r}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging the above into our expression for $V,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}V(r) & =\pi {r}^{2}(\frac{6}{r}-\frac{r}{2}) \\ V(r) & =(6r-\frac{{r}^{3}}{2})\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

We want to maximize $V,$ so we need to differentiate $V$ and set the derivative equal to zero. The derivative is 

$$
{V}^{′}(r)=(6-\frac{3{r}^{2}}{2})\pi .
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives a stationary point, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(r) & =0 \\ (6-\frac{3{r}^{2}}{2})\pi  & =0 \\ 6 & =\frac{3{r}^{2}}{2} \\ {r}^{2} & =4 \\ r & =2\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that, in the last step, we only considered the positive root because the radius $r$ must be positive.

Finally, we confirm that $r=2$ is a maximum using the second derivative test. The second derivative ${V}^{″}(r)$ is

$$
{V}^{″}(r)=\frac{-6\pi r}{2}=-3\pi r,
$$

and we can see that ${V}^{″}(2)<0.$ So, the stationary point $r=2$ is indeed a maximum of $V(r).$

So the cylinder with the largest volume has a radius of $r=2\,\text{cm}.$

Finally, to find the largest volume ${V}_{\text{max}},$ we substitute $r=2\,\text{cm}$ into the equation for the volume $V:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{max}}=V(2) & =(6(2)-\frac{1}{2}{(2)}^{3})\pi  \\  & =(12-4)\pi  \\  & =8\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$
